questions.question: Why is automated code review considered a 'force multiplier' rather than a replacement for human review?
choices: It catches 80% of trivial issues so humans can focus on architecture and logic
It eliminates the need for code review entirely
It only works on small codebases
questions.explanation: Automated review handles the obvious stuff (console.log, magic numbers, TODO comments) in milliseconds, freeing human reviewers to focus on deeper issues like design, correctness, and business logic.

questions.question: When parsing a diff, why must you strip the +/- prefix from each line before pattern matching?
choices: Regex patterns won't match text that starts with + or -
The prefixes cause the function to crash
questions.explanation: Diff lines start with '+' or '-' to indicate additions or removals. If you search for 'console.log' in a line like '+  console.log("test")', the pattern won't match because of the prefix characters.

questions.question: Why should common values like 0, 1, and -1 NOT be flagged as magic numbers?
choices: They are too small to matter
They are universally understood constants that don't need named constants
They only appear in test files
questions.explanation: Values like 0, 1, and -1 are so commonly used in programming (array indexing, boolean-like flags, loop counters) that extracting them to named constants would reduce readability rather than improve it.
